# Instruments: Drum kits

A note's `pitch` uses the **GM drum key**. Latest list: `muser instruments --family drums`.

| instrument | Recommended range | Polyphony | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `drums.808` | 35–81 | 24 | TR-808 style: long-tail low kick, crisp clap; hip-hop / trap / electronic |
| `drums.909` | 35–81 | 24 | TR-909 style: punchy kick and cymbals; house / techno |
| `drums.606` | 35–81 | 24 | TR-606 style: light and crisp; acid / electro |
| `drums.cr78` | 35–81 | 24 | CR-78 style: soft and vintage, with shaker, cowbell and bongos |
| `drums.acoustic` | 35–81 | 24 | Acoustic drum kit (physical modeling); pop / rock / jazz |
| `drums.trap` | 35–81 | 24 | trap kit: heavy kick, crisp snare and clap; suited to rapid closed-hat rolls |
| `drums.techno` | 35–81 | 24 | techno kit: kick with a rumbling tail, hard clap |
| `drums.house` | 35–81 | 24 | house kit: four-on-the-floor kick, clap, shaker, congas |
| `drums.dnb` | 35–81 | 24 | drum & bass kit: tight snare and deep kick |
| `drums.lofi` | 35–81 | 24 | lo-fi kit: soft, dark, with a 12-bit sampled texture |

## Adjustable parameters (instrument_params)

Override the sound of the chosen instrument/preset; write only the items you want to change, the rest stay as they are. `muser instruments <name>` shows the preset's current values.

Set per drum piece: { "kick": { "tune": -2, "decay": 1.5 }, "38": { "snap": 0.8 } }. Keys can be a GM drum key number or an alias (kick snare clap closed_hat open_hat crash ride tom_low tom_mid tom_high ...).

Each drum piece is adjustable (when automating, write `piece.parameter`, such as `kick.tune`; it takes effect from the next hit):

| Parameter | Range | Automation | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tune` | -24 – 24 st | next note | Drum piece tuning (semitones). Kick -3 is deeper; snare +2 is tighter |
| `decay` | 0.1 – 10 x | next note | Tail length (multiple of the original). 0.5 short; 2 longer (808 long-tail kick) |
| `level` | 0 – 4 x | next note | Volume (multiplier), 1 = unchanged |
| `tone` | 0 – 1 | next note | Tone (varies by drum piece, usually brightness) |
| `snap` | 0 – 1 | next note | Attack snap (varies by drum piece; snare wires for a snare) |
| `texture` | 0 – 1 | next note | Texture (varies by drum piece) |
| `pan` | -1 – 1 | next note | Pan: -1 left to 1 right |

### Tuning examples

- Deeper, longer kick, crisper snare, quiet closed hi-hat

  ```json
  { "instrument": "drums.808", "instrument_params": {"kick": {"tune": -3, "decay": 1.8}, "snare": {"snap": 0.8}, "closed_hat": {"level": 0.6}} }
  ```

## Common rhythm skeletons (4/4, one bar = 4 beats)

- Basic pop/rock: kick on 0, 2; snare on 1, 3; closed hi-hat every 0.5 beat.
- house/techno four-on-the-floor: kick on 0, 1, 2, 3; clap on 1, 3; open hi-hat at 0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5.
- trap (half-time feel): kick on 0, 1.75, 2.5; snare/clap on 2; closed hi-hat every 0.25 beat, with rolls of 0.125 beat in places.
- drum & bass: kick on 0, 2.5; snare on 1, 3; closed hi-hat every 0.5 beat.

## Tips and common mistakes

- A note's `pitch` is a **GM drum key**, not a scale pitch. Using 60 (middle C) triggers the high bongo (cr78 / acoustic) or makes no sound.
- For drum notes a `length` of 0.1-0.25 is enough; the ring-out of crash and open hi-hat is decided by the drum piece itself.
- An open hi-hat (46) followed right away by a closed hi-hat (42) or pedal hi-hat (44) chokes the open hi-hat; this is normal drum-machine behavior.
- Use velocity `velocity` for dynamics: strong beats 0.9-1.0, weak beats 0.6-0.8, ghost notes 0.3-0.4.
